description: Trade events/sec from a Kafka backlog to committed PostgreSQL rows.

environment.note: Single developer machine; PostgreSQL, Redis and a one-broker Kafka in Docker Desktop on the same host as the code under test, sharing its CPU and disk.

workload.mode: backlog drain: all events published before the consumer starts

configuration.log_level: WARNING (INFO in normal running; the consumer logs per batch at DEBUG)

does_not_prove: One consumer instance on one machine; it says nothing about how the rate scales with more consumers or partitions.
Trades only. Quotes and bars take different write paths and were not measured.
A backlog drain measures capacity, not end-to-end latency under a live feed — see the e2e_latency benchmark for that.
PostgreSQL, Kafka and the consumer shared one laptop's CPU and disk; a separate database host would change the figure in either direction.
